in_sanskrit.name: शर्वणी
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The one who brings abundance and prosperity, often in the form of rice and grain. Derived from the Sanskrit word 'sharva' meaning abundance and 'ani' meaning flow or giving.

in_hindi.name: शर्वणी
in_hindi.long_meaning: She who embodies completeness and happiness. In Hindu mythology, Sharvani is a form of the goddess Lakshmi, the deity of wealth and prosperity.

in_tamil.name: ஶர்வாலீ
in_tamil.long_meaning: She who brings abundance and prosperity to those around her. In Tamil mythology, Sharvali is a revered goddess who is invoked for success and prosperity.

in_telugu.name: శర్వణీ
in_telugu.long_meaning: She who is the embodiment of completeness and goddess of wealth and fortune. In Telugu mythology, Sharvani is an important deity worshipped for prosperity and good fortune.
